content: The community stagnates without the impulse of the individual. The impulse dies away without the sympathy of the community.
author: William James
sourceWork: Pragmatism: A New Name for Some Old Ways of Thinking (1907)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, William James saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
